questions.q: What does the Marks card control in Tableau?
options: How every mark in the view looks — its color, size, level of detail, and shape
Which fields are allowed to connect to the data source
The SQL query Tableau runs behind the scenes
Only whether the workbook is published to Tableau Server
questions.explain: The Marks card is the panel that controls the visual encoding of every mark — color, size, detail, shape, label, and tooltip.

questions.q: When you drop a continuous measure like Profit on Color, what happens?
options: Tableau scales every mark's shade along a color gradient based on that measure's value
Tableau ignores the field since Color only accepts dimensions
Every mark turns the same fixed color
The field is removed from the view entirely
questions.explain: A continuous (measure) field on Color produces a gradient legend, and each mark's shade reflects its own value within that range.

questions.q: What does the Detail property on the Marks card do?
options: Adds a field to the view's level of detail, splitting marks apart, without adding color or using a shelf
Makes marks bigger
Changes the mark type to a custom shape
Deletes duplicate marks from the view
questions.explain: Detail breaks marks apart by an additional dimension without visually encoding it as color, size, or shape — useful when you want granularity without more visual noise.

questions.q: If you want bars, circles, or lines to scale continuously based on a measure, which Marks card property do you use?
options: Size
Detail
Shape
Tooltip
questions.explain: Size is the property that scales marks continuously — either manually with the slider or automatically by dropping a measure onto it.

questions.q: What does the Shape property let you change?
options: The default circle or square mark to a custom shape, driven by a dimension
The color legend's number format
The font used in axis labels
The data source connection type
questions.explain: Shape swaps the mark's default appearance (like a circle) for a custom shape — categorical, driven by a dimension on the Shape shelf.
